Sodium content DERIVED, not measured: 22.99/58.44 = 39.339% of pure NaCl by mass, x 100 g = 39339 mg. Corrected 2026-07-31 from 38758, which was a measured table-salt value (implying ~98.5% NaCl purity) sitting under a note that claimed the stoichiometric derivation -- the number and its stated justification did not match. The derivation is chosen over the measured value for reproducibility: anyone can rederive it from two atomic masses, whereas the measured figure needs a source document nobody here has opened. NOTE THE COST: iodised table salt is NOT pure NaCl (anti-caking agents, potassium iodate, moisture), so this figure describes the derivation and overstates a real product's sodium by roughly 1.5%. It is a reproducible upper bound, not a product measurement. verified=false: no primary source has been opened for either figure

DIAAS 0.65 is AUTHORED, not sourced, and the recollection behind it is WIDE: published figures for soy foods recalled anywhere between roughly 0.5 for tofu and 0.9 for soy protein isolate, the spread depending on processing and on which reference amino-acid pattern was used. 0.65 sits near the low end of that spread, entered conservatively for the reason given on paneer_fresh. IFCT 2017 code M004 (Egg, poultry, whole, boiled), group M (Egg and Egg Products). PROVENANCE, composition (energy/protein/fat/carb/fibre/sodium/iron/calcium): retrieved 2026-08-16 from github.com/nodef/ifct2017 (compositions/index.csv) -- the CURRENTLY MAINTAINED mirror of the same Sahu & Sahu digitization used for rice_milled_raw/rajma_raw/toor_dal_raw/potato_raw, fetched via this mirror rather than the Zenodo release specifically because the Zenodo release's own compositions file (identical underlying data, larger single-file distribution) truncated before reaching group M under this build's fetch tooling on every mirror tried; nodef/ifct2017 is the actively-updated source repo those Zenodo snapshots are cut from, not a different dataset. Same underlying NIN measurement, second-party transcription, not the primary NIN-published IFCT2017.pdf -- not cross-checked against the PDF for transcription error. Raw source fields (per representations/index.csv, this build's own unit-conversion check against the source's declared units): enerc=618 kJ -> 147.7 kcal (÷4.184, same conversion implicitly reproduced by rice_milled_raw's 1491 kJ -> 356.4 kcal); protcnt=13.43 g, fatce=10.54 g read directly (factor 1); cho/choavldf/fibtg=0 g each (source's own values, not assumed); na=0.121 g -> 121.0 mg, fe=0.00187 g -> 1.87 mg, ca=0.05512 g -> 55.12 mg (all x1000 per the source's own g-to-mg representation factor). verified=false pending a human opening IFCT2017.pdf Table 1 (food-group M) at code M004 directly -- see docs/methodology.md. B12 GAP, FLAGGED NOT DEFAULTED: IFCT2017's compositions table has NO vitamin-B12/cobalamin column at all -- checked programmatically against all 421 column headers in the source file used above, zero matches for b12/cbl/cobal in any form. This is a structural gap in the source table (true for every food it lists, not specific to egg), not a value IFCT recorded as zero. b12_ug=1.11 for this row therefore comes from a DIFFERENT source, USDA FoodData Central, SR Legacy, FDC ID 173424 ('Egg, whole, cooked, hard-boiled'), fetched 2026-08-16 via api.nal.usda.gov -- a deliberate single-field exception to this row's otherwise-IFCT provenance, and must not be read as an IFCT figure. DIAAS 1.35 is SOURCED, not authored, unlike paneer_fresh/tofu_firm/soya_chunks_dry: Fanelli NS, Martins JCFR, Stein HH, 'The digestible indispensable amino acid score (DIAAS) in eggs and egg-containing breakfast meals is greater than in toast breads or hash browns served without eggs', Journal of Nutritional Science 2024;13:e68, DOI 10.1017/jns.2024.71 -- boiled egg DIAAS = 135% (1.35) under the >3-years-old reference amino-acid pattern (this project plans for adults, not infants; the paper's 6-36-month reference pattern gives 110% instead and is not used here).

IFCT 2017 code N003 (Chicken, poultry, breast, skinless, RAW), group N (Poultry). PROVENANCE, composition: retrieved 2026-08-16 from github.com/nodef/ifct2017 compositions/index.csv, same mirror and method as egg_boiled. Chosen over N001 (leg): N001's stated energy (1605 kJ) is roughly double what its own protein and fat account for under Atwater (191.5 kcal implied vs 383.6 kcal stated) -- an internal error in that row, found by this build's own Atwater reconciliation check, not used. N003 reconciles cleanly: 704 kJ = 168.3 kcal vs 168.2 kcal implied by 21.81 g protein + 9.0 g fat, 0.1 kcal off. Raw source fields: protcnt=21.81 g, fatce=9.0 g (factor 1); cho/choavldf/fibtg=0 g each; na=0.0367 g -> 36.7 mg, fe=0.00083 g -> 0.83 mg, ca=0.01291 g -> 12.91 mg (x1000). verified=false, same reasoning as every other IFCT-sourced row here. NO COOKED-STATE ENTRY EXISTS: IFCT2017's poultry group (N001-N019) is entirely raw-basis; no boiled/roasted chicken composition is tabulated anywhere in the source. This row is therefore used AS RAW for the finished (boiled) quantity in any recipe that uses it -- an approximation, not corrected by a yield/shrinkage factor, because none is registered in citations.py and none is sourced here. Cooked meat concentrates protein and fat per gram relative to raw (water is lost, mass is not replaced), so recipes using this row on a raw-composition basis UNDERSTATE the true finished-dish protein and fat per gram. Flagged here and in every recipe that uses it; not solved in this commit. B12: IFCT has no B12 column for any food (see egg_boiled's note); b12_ug=0.34 is USDA FoodData Central SR Legacy FDC ID 171477 ('Chicken, broilers or fryers, breast, meat only, cooked, roasted'), fetched 2026-08-16 -- a single-field exception, cooked-basis (the only chicken B12 figure readily available), while every other field on this row is raw-basis IFCT. DIAAS 1.10 IS DERIVED BY THIS BUILD, NOT QUOTED FROM A PUBLISHED SCORE -- one step below egg_boiled's and below the fish row's own sourcing. Digestibility (true ileal, dual-isotope, healthy Indian adults, pressure-cooked pooled breast/wing/thigh/drumstick -- the same preparation this project's chicken recipes use): methionine 92.7%, phenylalanine 94.4%, threonine 93.7%, lysine 95.5%, leucine 89.1%, isoleucine 88.8%, valine 89.6% from Kashyap S, Shivakumar N, Varkey A, Duraisamy R, Thomas T, Preston T, Devi S, Kurpad AV, 'Ileal digestibility of intrinsically labeled hen's egg and meat protein determined with the dual stable isotope tracer method in Indian adults', Am J Clin Nutr 2018;108(5):980-987, DOI 10.1093/ajcn/nqy178 (open access, CC BY 4.0); tryptophan 95.9% from the same lab's Kashyap S, Devi S, Pasanna RM, Preston T, Kurpad AV, 'True Digestibility of Tryptophan in Plant and Animal Protein', J Nutr 2024;154(11):3203-3209, DOI 10.1016/j.tjnut.2024.09.014 (Trp value read from the freely visible PubMed abstract; the paper's own DIAAS table is paywalled and was not reached). HISTIDINE IS UNASSESSED, NOT GUESSED: no digestibility figure for histidine was found in either paper. Amino-acid CONTENT (mg per g protein, needed to combine with the digestibility figures above): USDA FDC 171477, the same cooked chicken-breast item used for B12 above -- used instead of this row's own IFCT amino-acid columns because those columns failed a plausibility check (IFCT's own cysteine figure for this exact food, N003, implies ~92 mg cysteine per g protein; USDA's implies ~13 mg/g, and 13 mg/g is the biologically normal range -- IFCT's amino-acid columns are not used anywhere in this derivation as a result). Reference pattern: FAO Food and Nutrition Paper 92 (2013), 'Dietary protein quality evaluation in human nutrition: Report of an FAO Expert Consultation', Table 5, 'Older child, adolescent, adult' row (mg/g protein: His 16, Ile 30, Leu 61, Lys 48, SAA 23, AAA 41, Thr 25, Trp 6.6, Val 40) -- the same >3-years pattern egg_boiled's quoted DIAAS uses, sourced directly from the FAO PDF rather than a secondary citation. Sulphur (Met+Cys) and aromatic (Phe+Tyr) amino-acid GROUPS are scored using the single measured digestibility (methionine, phenylalanine respectively) applied to the whole group's content -- Cys and Tyr digestibility were not separately measured in either Kashyap paper, and this project's own DIAAS papers (Fanelli et al.) follow the same convention when only one group member is measured. Of the 8 amino acids with both a digestibility figure and a content figure, LEUCINE is limiting at 109.6% (valine close behind at 111.1%); DIAAS = 1.10, reported to 2 significant figures because the true score could move if histidine, once measured, turns out lower. Full per-amino-acid working is not repeated here; see docs/raw/ifct/README.md.

IFCT 2017 code P057 (Pomfret, white), group P (Marine Fish). PROVENANCE, composition: retrieved 2026-08-16 from github.com/nodef/ifct2017 compositions/index.csv, same mirror and method as egg_boiled/chicken_breast_raw. Reconciles cleanly under this build's Atwater check: 513 kJ = 122.6 kcal vs 122.2 kcal implied by 19.02 g protein + 5.12 g fat, 0.4 kcal off. Raw source fields: protcnt=19.02 g, fatce=5.12 g (factor 1); cho/choavldf/fibtg=0 g each; na=0.04609 g -> 46.09 mg, fe=0.00031 g -> 0.31 mg, ca=0.01364 g -> 13.64 mg (x1000). verified=false, same reasoning as every other IFCT-sourced row here. NO COOKED-STATE ENTRY EXISTS, same structural gap and same unresolved raw-basis approximation as chicken_breast_raw -- see that row's note; applies identically here and is not repeated in full. allergens=fish: pomfret is a finfish, a recognised major food-allergen category. B12: IFCT has no B12 column for any food; b12_ug=1.86 is USDA FoodData Central SR Legacy FDC ID 175177 ('Fish, tilapia, cooked, dry heat'), NOT pomfret -- pomfret is not in USDA's database, so tilapia (a lean whitefish, the closest available match) stands in for it, a second approximation layered on top of the single-field IFCT/USDA split used elsewhere. DIAAS 1.16 IS DERIVED BY THIS BUILD, NOT QUOTED, and rests on a CROSS-SPECIES SUBSTITUTION, named plainly rather than hidden: digestibility comes from Hodgkinson SM, Stroebinger N, Stein HH, Fanelli NS, de Vries S, van der Wielen N, Hendriks WH, Moughan PJ, 'True Ileal Amino Acid Digestibility of Human Foods Classified According to Food Type as Determined in the Growing Pig', J Nutr 2025;155:3384-3400 -- specifically its 'Fish, white' column (tilapia fillets, boiled 10 min then diced; identified as tilapia by elimination, since the same table carries separate 'Salmon' and 'Sardines' columns elsewhere and tilapia is the one lean white-fleshed fish of the three species the paper tested). Tilapia was chosen over salmon or sardines as the proxy for pomfret specifically because both tilapia and pomfret are lean, white-fleshed fish with a similar macro-composition (roughly 19-20% protein, under 6% fat) -- salmon and sardines are both notably fattier, oilier fish, a worse structural match. Amino-acid CONTENT is ALSO from tilapia (USDA FDC 175177, the same cooked item used for B12 above), not from this row's own IFCT amino-acid columns, for the same reason as chicken_breast_raw: this row's own IFCT phenylalanine figure implies ~64 mg/g protein against a biologically normal range of roughly 38-42 mg/g, so IFCT's amino-acid columns are not trusted here either. This DIAAS therefore describes TILAPIA throughout (digestibility and amino-acid content both), applied to pomfret as the best available proxy -- not a pomfret-specific measurement layered with a pomfret-specific composition. Reference pattern: same FAO 2013 Table 5 'older child, adolescent, adult' row as chicken_breast_raw and egg_boiled. All 9 indispensable amino acids have both a digestibility and a content figure for this food (no gap, unlike chicken); VALINE is limiting at 115.8%; DIAAS = 1.16. SAA and AAA groups scored the same single-measured-member-stands-for-the-group way as chicken_breast_raw. Full per-amino-acid working is not repeated here; see docs/raw/ifct/README.md.
